intended_object: The functor Div_{X/S} : (Sch/S)^op → Set of relative effective Cartier divisors of f : X → S, sending an S-scheme T to the set of relative effective Cartier divisors D ⊂ X_T = T ×_S X over T (effective Cartier with D → T flat), with maps given by pullback along X_{T'} → X_T. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation (Kleiman FGA 9.3, Stacks "Relative effective Cartier divisors").
explanation: The ambient functor `baseChangeIdealSheafFunctor f` sends T ∈ (Over S)^op to the ideal sheaves on `pullback T.hom f` = T ×_S X. Its action on morphisms is Mathlib's `IdealSheafData.comap` along the induced map X_{T'} → X_T. `comap` is the kernel of the fibre-product projection, so it is the scheme-theoretic pullback of closed subschemes, the correct functoriality. The subfunctor keeps, at T, the ideal sheaves I with `IsRelativeEffectiveCartier I (pullback.fst T.hom f)`. That predicate means I is effective Cartier (locally on affine opens generated by a single nonzerodivisor) and the composite D → X_T → T is flat. This is exactly the Stacks Project definition (tag 062T), which also imposes no flatness on X → S. The `map` field only proves the condition is stable under base change, so it does not affect the object defined. The construction is stated for an arbitrary morphism of schemes and arbitrary S-schemes T, which is its natural generality. Mathlib at this commit has no effective Cartier divisor functor, so there is no counterpart.
